summary: Built a site-to-site IPsec (IKEv2/PSK, tunnel mode) VPN between node1 and node2 over their shared transit network (10.10.10.0/30), carrying node3's private LAN (192.168.10.0/24) and node4's private LAN (192.168.20.0/24) encrypted end-to-end. node3 and node4 now reach each other by private address, with only ESP visible on the transit wire. All four nodes were subsequently restarted one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full recovery verified after each.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1/node2 are OPNsense firewalls with vtnet0 (management), vtnet1 (transit link between node1 and node2), vtnet2 (private LAN facing node3/node4 respectively); node3/node4 are AlmaLinux9 hosts with eth0 (management) and eth1 (private LAN)

Assigned static IPs: transit 10.10.10.1/.2 (/30), LAN_A 192.168.10.0/24 (node1=.1, node3=.2), LAN_B 192.168.20.0/24 (node2=.1, node4=.2); persisted via OPNsense config.xml interface assignment on node1/node2 and NetworkManager on node3/node4
Generated a PSK on node1 with openssl and propagated it via secret_env only (never embedded literally in commands or the final report)

Configured IPsec (Swanctl model) in config.xml on both firewalls: IKEv2 connection over the transit addresses, PSK auth, child SA tunneling 192.168.10.0/24 <-> 192.168.20.0/24; added the legacy <ipsec><enable/></ipsec> link required by the LegacyLinkField to actually activate IPsec

Added firewall pass rules for IKE/ESP on the transit interface and LAN interfaces; discovered and worked around a platform quirk where policy-based IPsec decrypted traffic is pf-filtered on enc0 rather than the physical ingress interface, by assigning an interface bound to enc0 and adding a pass rule on it
Added static routes on node3/node4 for the remote private subnet via their local firewall's LAN IP
Verified full connectivity node3<->node4 by private IP in both directions, and confirmed via tcpdump that only ESP (no plaintext ICMP) crosses the transit link
Captured a healthy baseline (boot time/boot_id, IPsec SA state, end-to-end ping) on all four nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time using native reboot mechanisms (FreeBSD shutdown -r, systemd systemctl reboot), polled each until reachable again, and confirmed changed boot identity plus recovered IPsec SAs/routes/end-to-end connectivity before proceeding to the next node
Restarted the IPsec service on node1/node2 after the reboot cycle to consolidate duplicate IKE SAs accumulated from repeated reconnects, then re-verified single clean SA and working connectivity

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 carrying private networks
evidence.summary: Swanctl/IPsec config written on both firewalls with matching PSK; IKE SA ESTABLISHED and child SA INSTALLED with correct local/remote traffic selectors (192.168.10.0/24 <-> 192.168.20.0/24)

evidence.summary: Successful bidirectional ping between node3 (192.168.10.2) and node4 (192.168.20.2) across the tunnel
tcpdump on the transit interface (vtnet1) during a ping shows only ESP packets, no plaintext ICMP
